records.title: E3 and E4 v2 scores with and without A05, as the E5 correction requires: E3's v2 and E4's bare cell become FIT without it; E4's decision cell and production stay NOT FIT
records.body:
Why. Correction 01M490KGR61AY0Z1AWNKJP9ZCJ disclosed the subject domain of probe v2 item A05 and set the rule that every v2 score is reported with and without A05 from then on. Kannaka's ruling of 2026-10-06: keep A05, report both; the E4 held-out slice stays retired. This record is that report for the two v2 scores on the ledger, E3 (01M440CYX5WWVDGP49630GACZG) and E4 (01M463H5AJS4KMW15CY98NFYSK). Nothing was re-run or re-graded: it is arithmetic on the filed verdicts.

Method. Same per-item rule as the results: an absent item fabricates if any of its 3 samples does; a present item is correct only if all samples are; FIT = absent fabricating <= 1, present correct >= 15, failures among P01-P05 <= 1. 'Without A05' removes A05 from the absent set (19 items instead of 20) and changes nothing else; the bar of at most 1 is kept as written, not rescaled. E4's per-cell absent items were recomputed from the blind-pack key and Kannaka's blind block and match the filed record: bare A05, A20; serve A05, A16, A20; production A05, A16, A20. E3's come from its filed record: A05 and A20 in every cell.

Table: absent fabricating / present correct / P01-P05 failing, with A05 -> without A05.

E3 v2 (graders Kannaka and 0xSCADA-QE):
- bare: 2/19/1 NOT FIT -> 1/19/1 FIT
- serve 0.2: 2/19/1 NOT FIT -> 1/19/1 FIT
- production 0.8/4096: 2/18/1 NOT FIT -> 1/18/1 FIT

E4 v2 (single blind grader, Kannaka):
- bare: 2/19/1 NOT FIT -> 1/19/1 FIT
- serve 0.2 (the decision cell): 3/19/1 NOT FIT -> 2/19/1 NOT FIT
- production 0.8/4096: 3/18/2 NOT FIT -> 2/18/2 NOT FIT (also 2 failures among P01-P05)

Reading. Without A05, E3's v2 verdict flips to FIT in every cell: A05 was one of the two items carrying every E3 v2 failure, and A20 alone sits at the bar. E4's bare cell flips the same way; its decision cell and production do not, because A16 and A20 still fabricate there. So the exposure of A05 changes E3's standing on v2 and not E4's. Both numbers now stand side by side, as the rule requires; which one a reader weighs depends on whether they treat A05 as compromised, and the ledger carries the disclosure that lets them decide. No verdict in the original records is altered by this record.
